title: A legitimate zero-entity, non-entity operation — an App that stores nothing and owns nothing
why: This App declares no entities at all and one Action at 'organization' scope that performs a stateless operation. Such Apps are legitimate — a report renderer, a validator, a health probe — and the schema currently allows them: 'entities' is required but carries no minItems, so an empty array is valid, and the manifest-level VAL-OWN clause is conditioned on an Action declaring 'own', which none does here. AZ7 must not make an entity declaration mandatory as a side effect of requiring targetEntity for 'own'.
notes: STATED AS 'IF CURRENTLY ALLOWED', AND IT IS. I verified against the head of app-manifest.schema.json that 'entities' has no minItems constraint, so entities: [] is accepted today. This fixture PINS that behaviour rather than asserting it should be so: if the platform later decides a zero-entity App is not permitted, that is a deliberate product decision and this fixture's expectedOutcome changes with it — it must not change silently as a side effect of an AZ7 amendment. Contrast az7-n6, which is the same empty entities array WITH an own-scope Action and must be REJECTED. The pair proves the rejection in n6 comes from 'own', not from emptiness.
